packageRules.description: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy publishes v1 as both a 2021 tag (1a947af9992250f3bc2e68ad0754c0b0c11566c9) and a 2024 branch head (4d27395796ac319302594769cfe812bd207490b1). Renovate's github-tags datasource resolves v1 to the tag, so an automated digest update would silently revert the pinned deploy step from the branch head back to 3.5-year-old code — see SECURITY-PIPELINE.md for the full analysis. This action has only ever published v1, so disabling updates here loses no legitimate version bump.

Tailwind CSS v4 is deferred until the Create React App to Vite migration lands. v4 moves the PostCSS plugin into a separate @tailwindcss/postcss package and requires the PostCSS configuration to be rewritten -- PR #56 failed to compile on exactly that. Doing the rewrite under CRA would be throwaway work, because the Vite setup replaces the PostCSS wiring with the @tailwindcss/vite plugin rather than porting it. Left enabled, Renovate re-opens the same PR every cycle, it fails the build every time, and it holds one of ten Static Web Apps staging slots while doing so. Minor and patch updates to tailwindcss are unaffected; only the major is held. Re-enable this rule as part of the Vite migration.

TypeScript v7 is deferred until the Create React App to Vite migration lands. react-scripts@5.0.1 peer-requires typescript "^3.2.1 || ^4", so npm cannot resolve v7 at all -- PR #58 shipped a package.json bump with no lockfile, because Renovate's lockfile generation failed against that peer constraint, and every build then died on `npm ci` with "lock file's typescript@4.9.5 does not satisfy typescript@7.0.2". The out-of-sync lockfile is the symptom; react-scripts is the cause, and nothing in the pull request can fix it. Forcing it through with --legacy-peer-deps would paper over a real incompatibility rather than resolve it. Vite does not constrain the TypeScript version the way react-scripts does, so this unblocks itself once the migration lands. Minor and patch updates to typescript are unaffected; only the major is held. Re-enable this rule as part of the Vite migration, alongside the tailwindcss rule above.

@vitejs/plugin-react v6 is deferred until the Create React App to Vite migration lands. v6 pulls @rolldown/plugin-babel, whose peers require Babel 8 (@babel/core and @babel/plugin-transform-runtime at "^7.29.0 || ^8.0.0-rc.1"), while react-scripts@5.0.1 holds the tree on Babel 7 -- so npm cannot resolve it at all and `npm ci` dies with ERESOLVE before a single test runs. PR #71 failed on exactly that, within minutes of the phase 1 pull request that introduced the dependency. Nothing in such a pull request can fix it; react-scripts is the cause, and forcing it through with --legacy-peer-deps would paper over a real incompatibility rather than resolve it. This is the same shape as the tailwindcss and typescript rules above, and it unblocks itself the same way: phase 3 deletes react-scripts, and with it the Babel 7 constraint. Minor and patch updates to @vitejs/plugin-react are unaffected; only the major is held. Re-enable this rule as part of the Vite migration, alongside the two rules above.
